info.text:
Saving for 10 years starting at 25 can beat saving for 30 years starting at 35, and this video shows the exact math. Starting from the median full-time paycheck ($1,251 a week in Q2 2026, BLS), we work through a $60,000 salary saving 10% versus 15%, the compound growth formula, starting at 25 versus 35, the employer match, how a 1% fee compares with 0.05% over 30 years, emergency funds, credit card interest, lifestyle creep and the 2026 401(k) and IRA limits. We finish with the honest caveats: real S&P 500 returns from 2000 to 2025, including 2008 and the lost decade. All growth examples assume 7% a year after inflation, which is an assumption, not a promise.

Sources: BLS, Usual Weekly Earnings, Q2 2026 (July 2026); BEA, Personal Income and Outlays, August 2026 (Sept 2026); Vanguard, How America Saves 2026 (June 2026); Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of US Households in 2025 (May 2026); Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit (Oct 2026); IRS 2026 contribution limits (Nov 2025); ICI expense ratio report (2025); Aswath Damodaran, NYU Stern historical returns 1928-2025; Dimensional Fund Advisors (2000-2009 returns); S&P 500 annual total returns via YCharts. Growth math is our own calculation with the future-value formula.

News and education, not financial advice.
